description: Handle the moment a secret or private internal detail — an API key, cloud credential, internal hostname/domain, internal IP, or PII — turns up committed into a Git repo's *history*, not just the working tree, especially if public or about to be pushed publicly. Use when the user says "I found an API key in an old commit," "there's a secret in git history," "we committed a .env file years ago," "this internal IP/hostname leaked into a public repo," "how do I purge history before pushing," or "someone found a credential in our commit log." Also use for a pre-publish history sweep before open-sourcing. Covers in order: scan full history and show findings before touching anything; verified backup before any rewrite; rewrite safely, never `--no-verify`; verify real repo visibility before any push, never guessed from the URL; re-scan after rewrite, not trusting a clean `git log`; and what a rewrite never fixes alone — rotate any credential that was ever live, and disclose that forks keep the old history regardless.
